paper_title: NExtLong Toward Effective Long-Context Training without Long Documents
caption: NExtLong reduces the model's dependence on proximal text. We calculated the degree of dependence on proximal text (the last third of the text) for different methods when completing the LongQA task. It can be observed that NExtLong significantly reduces the model's dependence on proximal text.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the "Short-Dependence Attention Weight" for five different methods—Standard, ICLM, KNN, Quest, and NExtLong—evaluated on the LongQA task, with the vertical axis representing attention weight ranging from 0.80 to 0.90 in increments of 0.02 and the horizontal axis listing the methods. All bars are rendered in light blue and are of similar height, indicating comparable levels of short-dependence attention across most methods, except for NExtLong, which stands out as significantly lower. Specifically, Standard, KNN, and Quest each exhibit attention weights near 0.865, ICLM is slightly lower at approximately 0.855, and NExtLong is notably reduced to around 0.825. This visual comparison supports the paper’s claim that NExtLong reduces the model’s reliance on proximal text (defined as the last third of the input), as reflected in its substantially lower attention weight compared to the other methods. The chart’s legend identifies the light blue bars as representing “Short-Dependence Attention Weight,” and the overall layout includes gridlines to aid in value estimation.
